ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: More details of the methods used can be found in the Canada Dental Benefit -Expanded Baseline Survey Final Report. 10 Data were accessed from the Government of Canada Publications website, at: https://epe.bac-lac.gc.ca/100/200/301/pwgsc-tpsgc/por-ef/health/2024/014-23-e/014-23_Report.pdf. 11 Institutional ethics approval from the University of Manitoba was deemed unnecessary, as this study used aggregated and anonymized data without personal identifiers.
table.formatted: More details of the methods used can be found in the Canada Dental Benefit -Expanded Baseline Survey Final Report. <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">10</ref> Data were accessed from the Government of Canada Publications website, at: <ref type="url" target="https://epe.bac-lac.gc.ca/100/200/301/pwgsc-tpsgc/por-ef/health/2024/014-23-">https://epe.bac-lac.gc.ca/100/200/301/pwgsc-tpsgc/por-ef/health/2024/014-23-</ref>e/014-23_Report.pdf. <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">11</ref> Institutional ethics approval from the University of Manitoba was deemed unnecessary, as this study used aggregated and anonymized data without personal identifiers.

table.text: Quota sampling was employed for the base sample (n= 2,150) to ensure broad representation of Canadian adults who met the eligibility requirements of the CDCP, and eligible families from remote communities were recruited by telephone (n=100).
Most participants had completed post-secondary education (67.1%) and lived in urban centres (82.6%).
Married (or in common-law) participants were significantly more motivated to apply for the CDCP, when compared to those never married and those divorced or separated.

Married/common-law participants were significantly more motivated if they had more than one child in need of dental care (78.2%), if the program was recommended by their child's healthcare provider (76.4%), if their child had urgent dental needs (73.2%), and by the prospect of better dental health for their family (57.3%).

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Quota sampling was employed for the base sample (n= 2,150) to ensure broad representation of Canadian adults who met the eligibility requirements of the CDCP, and eligible families from remote communities were recruited by telephone (n=100).

> Most participants had completed post-secondary education (67.1%) and lived in urban centres (82.6%).

> Married (or in common-law) participants were significantly more motivated to apply for the CDCP, when compared to those never married and those divorced or separated.

> Married/common-law participants were significantly more motivated if they had more than one child in need of dental care (78.2%), if the program was recommended by their child's healthcare provider (76.4%), if their child had urgent dental needs (73.2%), and by the prospect of better dental health for their family (57.3%).

Ethics approval statement:

> More details of the methods used can be found in the Canada Dental Benefit -Expanded Baseline Survey Final Report. 10 Data were accessed from the Government of Canada Publications website, at: https://epe.bac-lac.gc.ca/100/200/301/pwgsc-tpsgc/por-ef/health/2024/014-23-e/014-23_Report.pdf. 11 Institutional ethics approval from the University of Manitoba was deemed unnecessary, as this study used aggregated and anonymized data without personal identifiers.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
